confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on two web searches. One looked up the RBA rate. The other pulled aggregated cost-of-living summaries for Bled from Numbeo, citycost, Wise, Lonely Planet and similar sites. Those sources gave a cappuccino at about EUR 1.9-2.5, a draft beer at about EUR 3.2-3.5, an inexpensive meal at about USD 12 and a mid-range dinner for two at about EUR 40-55. I raised all of these for Bled's lakeside tourist pricing in peak July 2026. I converted euros to US dollars at about 1.10 USD per EUR. That rate is implied by search-reported RBA cross rates for 18 Nov 2026 (1 AUD = 0.6720 USD and 0.6115 EUR). I did not check the EUR rate on rba.gov.au. The searches did not find direct aggregated prices for cocktails or wine. I estimated those from typical Slovenian price ratios to beer, so they are less certain. All four accommodation anchors are general-knowledge model estimates for a small, high-demand Alpine resort in peak summer. I did not search for accommodation prices or check any live listings. Actual July prices may vary widely, so accommodation is the least certain part of the estimate. The FX observation comes from a search summary that cited rba.gov.au. I did not open the RBA page itself.
comparable_city_reasoning: Bled is a small, heavily touristed lake resort in the Slovenian Alps. I treated its prices as above Ljubljana's and roughly like Hallstatt-lite or Croatian coastal resort towns, though cheaper than Austrian Alpine resorts.
